title: The therapeutic potential of psilocybin: a systematic review | Request PDF
abstract:
Classical psychedelics, such as psilocybin are notable both for their intense and remarkable psychoactive effects (e.g., enhanced self-awareness and mystical experiences [2]) and for their emerging therapeutic effects across a range of mental health and addiction conditions, including end-of-life anxiety, major depression, obsessive-compulsive disorder, alcohol use disorder and smoking cessation

Introduction: Psychedelic drugs were used quite extensively before their prohibition in 1968 which delayed research. However, since the 1990s studies on the potential therapeutic benefits of psychedelics rapidly increased. Areas covered: This systematic review provides an overview of the clinical effects of psilocybin in the treatment of a variety of mental disorders.
The present review supports this, similarly to previous systematic reviews which have assessed this drug's use for several mental health disorders [38, 39], as well as individually on MDD [40]. The included up to date studies in the present review therefore are in accordance with the notion of psilocybin being a potential therapeutic agent for MDD. ... Despite this, profound findings into its antidepressant effects (largely through its action on 5-HT1a receptors) in mental illnesses such as major depressive disorder have rapidly increased interest back into their potential therapeutic benefits. This systematic review provides an analysis of the studies examining the clinical use of psilocybin for major depressive disorder.
